stem: A post-incident review finds two components in an otherwise redundant stack that would each take down the whole application if they failed alone: a single EC2 instance running outside any Auto Scaling group, and a database with no standby. Which TWO fixes remove them? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: Add an Application Load Balancer with health checks in front of the single instance, without placing it in an Auto Scaling group.
Place the instance in an Auto Scaling group that spans multiple Availability Zones.
Enable Multi-AZ for the database instance.
Take a manual snapshot of the database on a fixed schedule.
Add a read replica to the database for reporting queries.

rationale: Placing the instance in an Auto Scaling group spanning multiple Availability Zones means a healthy replacement can launch in another zone if the original instance or its zone fails, removing that single instance as a point of failure. Enabling Multi-AZ gives the database an automatic-failover standby in a second Availability Zone, so the loss of the primary's zone no longer takes the database down. A load balancer's health check can stop sending traffic to the instance if it fails a check, but with no Auto Scaling group there is still only one instance behind it, so its failure still takes the application down. A scheduled snapshot protects against data loss and supports point-in-time restore, but restoring from a snapshot takes time and does not provide the automatic failover that removes this single point of failure. A read replica offloads read traffic but is not designed to fail over automatically, so it does not replace the automatic-failover protection the database is missing.
